Jericoacoara is a place of ocean views, white sand dunes, palm trees, and a small coastal village. Jericoacoara National Park lies nearby.

An active itinerary can include buggy rides, horseback riding, and schooner trips. Another route crosses beaches and dunes to Lago Azul and Lago Paraiso, while the coastline offers opportunities for surfing and other water activities.

Jericoacoara suits both relaxing getaways and active days. Beaches, dunes, lagoons, and trips around the area are easy to alternate without a packed schedule.

Jesús is associated with a Jesuit mission that became part of the history of Paraguay and the Guaraní people. The surviving buildings reveal the layout of a religious and social center. Stone walls and mission spaces evoke life in an organized community.

Jesús de Tavarangue forms part of UNESCO heritage together with the mission at Trinidad. Visitors explore both sites, comparing the remains of their churches and town layouts. These places offer insight into cultural encounters during the colonial period, when religion, music, crafts, and agriculture were interconnected within a mission.

Jougla Point lies on the western edge of Wiencke Island in Port Lockroy harbor. The uneven rocky shore is indented with small coves, while glaciers and steep snowy slopes rise around the harbor. Early in the season, fast ice may still surround the coast. During a landing, visitors can see traces of the area's whaling past, including whale bones.

Gentoo penguins and blue-eyed shags nest on the point, and Weddell seals come ashore. Expedition guides choose a suitable area for walking with regard to wildlife and shore conditions. Nesting areas are closed to visitors, while glaciers and snow-covered slopes require specialist equipment. Landings depend on the weather.
